method.data: IRSA cutouts (3.6', 35 px) of every SPHEREx DR1 image in IRSA's 3I/ATLAS table, centred on NASA's comet position; centroid within 2 px (else forced at NASA's position); apertures [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0] px (6.15"/px), sigma-clipped median background in a 12-17 px annulus; points with a mask bit within 2 px dropped. No aperture correction (extended coma; the core's 1.033 is applied at r = 2 px only).
method.scaling: each point scaled to the visit's median r and Delta by (r/r0)^2 (Delta/Delta0), the fixed-angular-aperture dependence of both dust (Afrho) and gas (rho << L) fluxes.
method.band_excess: a straight-line continuum fitted to side windows next to each band; excess = mean residual f_lambda in the band x band width = integrated band flux (W m^-2).
method.production_rate: N = 4 pi Delta^2 F / (g h nu), g = g1 / r^2; Haser parent with v = 0.85 r^-0.5 km/s and L = v tau1 r^2; the share of the column removed by the background annulus is added back with the same Haser model. g1 (photons/s/molecule at 1 au): CO2 2.6e-3, CO 2.6e-4, H2O 2.9e-4 (Crovisier 1997, as in Lisse et al.). tau1 (s, quiet Sun, Huebner et al. 1992): CO2 5.0e5, CO 1.3e6, H2O 8.3e4.
method.errors: err_w_m2 = measurement errors + side-window jitter (stars crossing the aperture, activity) through the trapezoid weights, plus the continuum error; snr = flux / err_w_m2 (detection significance). err_total_w_m2 adds 15% for the sparse channel sampling. Q_err_per_s scales err_total_w_m2; the g-factors, lifetimes and v add a factor ~2 systematic.
method.geometry: JPL Horizons C/2025 N1, geocentre (SPHEREx is in low Earth orbit).
